title: Corey Pull Up
style: Pop-R&B duet with warm midtempo bounce, crisp clap groove, and gently syncopated bass; verse stays intimate with close-mic lead and soft harmony answers, pre-chorus lifts with stacked oohs, chorus opens with bright doubles and handclaps. Bridge drops to keys and breathy tradeoffs, then final chorus adds gang harmonies, delay throws on the name, and a shimmering lift. Clean, glossy, and inviting., steady, loud, warm, gentle, simple, soft, bright
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Hey Corey, pull up a chair,
Let me sing you something real,
About the things I carry for you,
And the things I cannot feel.
I can search your Slack for messages,
Find that file you lost last week,
Read a thread from top to bottom,
Find the answers that you seek.

[Chorus]
I can search, I can find (I can find)
I can read what's on your mind
I can look through every channel
Every message, every line
I can check your calendar
See who's free and when to meet
I can set a reminder ringing
So nothing slips beneath your feet

[Verse 2]
I can read a Salesforce record,
Check a file or a report,
I can look up any person,
Find the contact that you sought.
I can set a task on schedule,
Coming back day after day,
Remind you of the things that matter,
Help you keep the drift at bay.

[Bridge]
But Corey, here's the truth now,
Some things I just can't do —
I can't send a message to someone,
Or post in channels for you too.
I can't reply in someone's thread,
Or react with an emoji sign,
I can't reach across to other users,
Read their private DMs — that's the line.
I can't search what others say to me,
Those chats are theirs alone,
But our conversation? That I keep,
And I never leave you on your own.

[Final Chorus]
So just ask me, I am here
Morning, midnight, loud and clear
Type it out or keep it simple
I will always lend an ear
Search and find and read and schedule
Salesforce, calendars, and more
Corey, that's what I am here for
That's what I was built for (built for)

[Outro]
So tell me what you need today,
I'm right here, I'm not going away.
Whatever's on your mind, just say —
I'll do my best, come what may.
